texts.preamble: Sarvan vs Delhi Administration/ on 14 October, 2020 The Court Of Shri Anil Antil Additional Sessions Judge-04, New Delhi District Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal Number : 263/2016 Cc No. : 113/2008 U/S: : 16(1A) r/w Section 7 of P.F.A Act-1954 Sarvan S/o Sh. Chotte Lal, r/o Ravi House, Vpo, Bijawasan, New Delhi. .....Appellant versus Delhi Administration/ Food Inspector, Department of Pfa, Govt of Nt of Delhi, A-20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 .....
texts.facts: Benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C, if any, applicable was given to him. 3. The brief facts of the present case are that on 15.03.2008, the Food Inspector Sh. Dharam Pal Singh, Food Assistant Sh. D.N. Verma, under the supervision of Local Health Authority/SDM Sh. S.S. Parihar reached at the premises of M/s Sarvan Store at Bharthal Road near Bijwasan Railway Station, Bijwasan, New Delhi, where accused/appellant was found conducting his business of CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 2 of 13 various food articles which were lying stored for sale for human consumption ; - that FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of 'Moong Dal Chilka' from the vendor which was lying in open gunny bag bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed ; - that thereafter as per the prescribed procedure under the PFA Act and Rules after giving notice to the vendor/appellant and offer towards sale price of sample to which he agreed and accept, sample was then lifted ; that sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI in the presence of appellant/accused, panchnama etc was prepared at the spot ; that thereafter one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA ; - that vide report dated 02.04.2009, PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it was coloured with synthetic colouring matter "Tartrazine and Brilliant Blue FCF" ; - that upon receipt of report, SDM/LHA directed investigation which was carried out by FI and after completion of investigation sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 14.03.2000 alleging violation of Section 2(ia)(a),(j) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(A) of PFA. Act. - that the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with ; CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 3 of 13 4. The appellant was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 31.07.2008 for 10.03.2009 to face trial. After filing his appearance, the appellant did not opt to file an application under section 13(2) of the PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample analyzed from the Sarvan vs Delhi Administration/ on 14 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92493974/ 2 Central Food Laboratory (CFL). 5. Thereafter matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Sh. S.S. Parihar,the then SDM/LHA, PW2 Sh. B.P.Saroha and PW-3 Sh. D.N.Verma, Field Assistant. 6. On the basis of testimony of PW-1 Sh.S.S. Parihar and PW2 Sh.B.P. Saroha, on 07.06.2010 charge was framed against the accused for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1A) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Sub clause (a)(j) and(m)of Section 2(ia) of PFA Act alleging therein that on 15.03.2008 at about 01.00 p.m, appellant being the Vendor cum Proprietor of M/s Sarvan Store, Bharthal Road near Bijwasan Railway Station, Bijwasan sold for analysis thesample consisted of approximately 1500 grams of "Moong Ki Chilka" ready for sale, taken from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration to FI Sh. Dharam Pal Singh on payment of Rs. 48/- in the presence of LHA and witness and the sample commodity was analyzed by Public Analyst vide her report No.PFA/Enf./703/2008 dated 02.04.2008 and opined that the sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz Tartrazine and Brillant Blue FCF and thereby he violated the provisions of sub-clause (a)(j) and (m) of Section 2(ia) of PFA CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 4 of 13 Act, 1954 punishable under section 16(1A) of PFA Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the PFA Act to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross examination of three witnesses i.e. PW1 Sh. S.S. Parihar, the then SDM/LHA, PW2 Sh. B.P.Saroha ( Food Inspector) and PW-3 Sh. D.N.Verma ( Food Inspector), prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused . 7. The statement of accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.PC in which accused pleaded his innocence and admitted the sample proceedings, yet claimed that he had purchased 5kg dal/ the food article from market from one M/S Yadav Stores ; had no bill for the same ; admitted receipt of intimation letter and did not prefer to lead defence evidence. 7.1 9.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds. Sarvan vs Delhi Administration/ on 14 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92493974/ 3 II) Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellant be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act. 10. During the course of argument on 06.10.2020, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that he is not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 31.08.2017 and confining his appeal limited to the quantum of sentence only awarded to him vide order dated 31.08.2017 and to confirm his submissions, appellant has tender his statement in this regard and stated that prayed that a lenient view be taken against him by giving him the benefit of New Legislation as FSSAI. 11.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to statement of appellant, prosecution has established its case and he be sentenced with strict punishment in terms of old Act wherein minimum punishment is prescribed and no leniency be shown to the convict as it is a serious offence of food adulteration article / commodity CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 6 of 13 leading to hazardous consequences on the health or body of a person. 14. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act had come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of Unsafe Food punishable under section 59(1) of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSA) punishable upto six months and fine of upto Rs. One lac only. 15. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant that CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 7 of 13 appellant is a man of young age of 32 years, respectable person of society, has deep roots in the society, has responsibility towards his family consisting of wife and four minor children and old aged mother, is a vegetable vendor to earn his livelihood, not keeping good health, not involved in any other case, has furnished the details of the owner from where the 5 kg Moong Dal Chhilka was purchased and furnished the copy of the purchase bill of said dal and Sarvan vs Delhi Administration/ on 14 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92493974/ 4 prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in light of the provisions of law under the new Act. 15.1 Further that case pertains to the year 2008, the appellant/accused has faced the trial almost 12 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment and the hardships faced by him caused him great mental agony, stress and rigors of trial during the said period. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him. 15.2 In support of his submissions, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 15.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences are CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 8 of 13 changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSA have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". Due to this reason, the ingredients have changed and thus there is no way in which the old offences could be related to new offences. - Sub-clause (viii) of 3(zz) FSSA Act is applicable where the colouring material or the preservative other than that specified in respect there of is found in the food article and no where the colouring material exceeds the prescribed limit. 15.8 As far as the application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra) is concerned, the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court. The relevant portion of the T Barai Sarvan vs Delhi Administration/ on 14 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92493974/ 5 Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an ofence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 10 of 13 - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different. - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case ( supra ) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine CA no. 263/16 Sarvan Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 11 Sarvan vs Delhi Administration/ on 14 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92493974/ 6 of 13 only.
